findings.name: A thread waits for a signal that already came
findings.impact: A thread signalled while nobody was waiting, so the signal was thrown away; the thread that waits afterwards sleeps for good, and whoever waits for it hangs too.
findings.summary: work_daemon[2] signalled condition variable 0x00000055c7fe7128 at 10363.16 ms when no thread was waiting on it, then joined work_daemon[3]. work_daemon[3] only began its wait 105.32 ms later and was still blocked 5667.81 ms on, until the process was torn down, with no further signal: the program is hung.
findings.qnx: pthread_cond_signal() wakes a thread that is already waiting; with no waiter the signal is lost. Wait in a loop that re-checks the condition while holding the mutex (the thread that sets the condition must also hold the mutex), and test the stop flag before every wait.

radar.name: work_daemon[3]
radar.summary: work_daemon[3] (prio 10) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 288 of its 331 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 80 ms. It stands out in: time waiting on a condition variable (higher than healthy), longest single block (higher than healthy), time asleep (lower than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is priority inversion while waiting on a condition variable, but only loosely (distance 9.83 against 0.847 typical for it): treat this as behaviour of its own.

radar.name: work_daemon[4]
radar.summary: work_daemon[4] (prio 10) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 308 of its 309 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 6140 ms. remedies.title: Re-check 'do_run_logger_thread' under the lock before the wait: if ((watcher_count == 0) && do_run_logger_thread)
remedies.rationale: pthread_cond_signal() wakes only a thread that is already waiting. The stopper sets the flag and signals under the mutex, but the waiter tests only its own idle condition before it waits, so a stop that lands while the waiter is not yet waiting is lost and the waiter sleeps forever. Testing the flag under the same mutex, in the same condition that guards the wait, makes the two orderings equivalent: either the waiter sees the flag and skips the wait, or it is already waiting when the signal arrives.
